questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.** 

It was by real sorrow (1)/ that I heard this morning (2)/ of your great loss. (3)/ No error
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **1**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

Reading the above sentence we find that:

__
 
• The error lies in the** first part **of the sentence. 
 
• Here the preposition **'by' **is **incorrect **and should be replaced with **'with'**.
 
• In the above sentence, the **manner or attitude in which the person heard something** is mentioned. 
 
• The correct preposition that indicates this **manner or attitude** is **'with'**. 
 
 
• **Example**: *The people shouted with pleasure.*
 
 

*​*Thus the error lies in the first part and therefore, it is the correct answer. 

The **correct sentence** is: *It was with real sorrow that I heard this morning of your great loss. *

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

__
 
• ***The uses of preposition with__***
 
• With means ‘in the same place as someone or something’ or ‘accompanying’:
 
 
• For example: She arrived with her boyfriend.
 
 
 
• With often follows adjectives which refer to reactions and feelings:
 
 
• For example: Are you happy with your music lessons?
 
 
 
• We use with to refer to what we use to do something:
 
 
• For example: They opened the package with a knife.
 
 
 
• We use with to mean ‘having’ or ‘possessing’:
 
 
• For example: It’s the house with the really big gates.
 
 
 
• We use with to mean ‘because of’ or ‘as a result of’. This is especially common in speaking:
 
 
• For example: With all this work, I’d better stay in tonight.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.** 

Angela was ________ of that big mansion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Terrified**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Let's look at the meaning of the given words. 

__
 
• **Terrified**​: Cause to feel extreme fear. 
 
• **Moisturised**: Make something less dry. 
 
• **Embarrassed**: Feeling or showing embarrassment. 
 
• **Sweating**: Exuding sweat profusely. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

From the given meanings only the word **terrified **fits the sentence contextually. 

 
• Angela was **terrified **of that big mansion.

 
 
• Which means that she was extremely scared of the big mansion. 
 
 

Thus the correct answer is **Terrified**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.** 

Jettison
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Eject**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at the meanings of the given word and the correct option:
 
• **Jettison**: To drop or get rid of something; to omit or forgo something. 
 
 
• Example: The station has **jettisoned **educational broadcasts.
 
 
 
• **Eject**: To throw something out; to get rid of something. 
 
 
• Example: Small splatters of molten lava were **ejected **from the crater.
 
 
 
• Thus form the given meanings we find that both the words express similar meanings. 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **Eject**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the **meanings **of the other given options. 
 
• **Keep**: Have or retain possession of. 
 
 
• Example: Do you want this photograph back or can I **keep **it?
 
 
 
• **Embrace**: Hold in one's arm; to accept something. 
 
 
• Example: This was an opportunity that he would **embrace**.
 
 
 
• **Retain**: Continue to have; or keep possession of. 
 
 
• Example: She has lost her battle to **retain **control of the company.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**** **

The economic

P: a country leads to exponential

Q: growth of that country

R: empowerment of women of
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **RPQ**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

Reading the above-given statements we find that: 

 
• Statement R is the first statement as it gives meaning and carries forward the given phrase **The economic**. 
 
• That is **The economic empowerment of women**. 
 
• The next statement to follow **R **is **P**. **P **gives more meaning to the statement **R. **
 
• It tells us specifically which women are to be empowered. 
 
• That is '**women of a country...**' 
 
• The next statement to follow **P **is **Q**. **Q **gives more meaning to the statement **R**.
 
• It tells us what the empowerment of women of a country leads to. 
 
• That is the 'g**rowth of that country**' 

Thus the correct answer is **RPQ**

***The economic empowerment of women of a country leads to exponential growth of that country.***

questions.question:
A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.

The commotion terrified her.

options.text: She was terrified by the commotion.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **She was terrified by the commotion**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Reading the above sentence we find that it is in the **Active voice. **

 
• While changing the sentence to **Passive voice **we have to reverse the subject and the object of the sentence. 
 
• The subject in the given sentence is **commotion **and the object is **her**. 
 
• Reversing both the subject and the object we get the sentence:
 
• Her changes to She and becomes the new subject. 

Thus the correct sentence will be: She was terrified by the commotion.

The Buddha (was consumed) by the human suffering that he saw all around him.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**No improvement**'.

• The sentence is in past tense, and we know this by the phrase '**he saw**'.
 
• Also the pronoun '**he**' which is **singular **is referring to '**The Buddha**'.

• Thus, the correct sentence- *The Buddha was consumed by the human suffering that he saw all around him.*
 
• Hence, the correct answer is** option 4**.
